articles.title: From Single Impact Sites to Dispersed Corridors: A Disaster Report of Emergency Medical Services Command Adaptation to Cluster-Munition Pattern Missile Strikes in Israel.
articles.abstract: This Disaster Report describes a series of missile impact events managed by Magen David Adom (MDA), Israel's national Emergency Medical Services (EMS) organization, during the March 2026 missile campaign. The report focuses on a recurring operational distinction between compact single-warhead impact events and dispersed cluster-munition pattern events. Unlike routine mass-casualty incident recognition, MDA dispatch did not need to infer the possibility of a dispersed event only from accumulating emergency calls. While missiles are in flight, the Home Front Command (HFC) broadcasts real-time threat alerts through multiple public channels: the official HFC app, direct cell broadcasts to all phones in the threatened area, and live overlays on all television channels. Command and dispatch personnel from MDA used this publicly available information as an early threat layer at or before the initial dispatch phase. Emergency calls, motorcycle first-responder reports, volunteer responder reports, and ambulance crew updates then refined the actual medical footprint. Across six events, cluster-munition pattern events involved four-to-six municipalities and maximum geographic spread of 6.9km to 11.5km, whereas single-warhead events remained within one municipality and had maximum geographic spread of less than 400 meters. The events suggest that dispersed missile attacks require EMS command to combine prehospital warning-system visibility with a distributed responder network that functions as a forward sensor layer for dispatch and command.

articles.title: Head, face, and neck injury patterns across the life course: a 20-year NEISS analysis of 2,345,287 emergency department visits in the U.S.
articles.abstract: Head, face, and neck injuries impose a substantial burden for emergency departments (ED); the mechanisms driving them across the life course however remain poorly understood at the population level. Large-scale, integrated analysis spanning anatomical regions, injury mechanisms, age groups, settings, and associated products or environmental surfaces offers an opportunity to identify the patterns and vulnerable populations that smaller or shorter-term studies cannot resolve. We queried National Electronic Injury Surveillance System (NEISS) records from 2006 to 2025 for injuries to the head, face, eyes, mouth, neck, or ears. Demographics, anatomical region, injury setting, associated products or environmental surfaces, and ED disposition were extracted, and a rule-based narrative classifier assigned 1 of 17 injury mechanisms from free-text descriptions. Non-routine ED disposition was defined as admission, transfer, observation, or fatality. Analyses were descriptive and based on unweighted NEISS case records. Among 2,345,287 ED presentations, representing 31.8% of all NEISS-coded visits, the head was most often injured (51.2%), followed by the face (28.2%). Annual volume rose 35.2% (105,727 in 2006 to 142,918 in 2025), driven mainly by head injuries (+ 83.4%). Median age was 14 years and 56.4% of patients were male, but among older adults (≥ 65 years), females predominated (60.6%). Falls were the leading mechanism (53.0% across subcategories). Most patients were treated and discharged (89.4%) and admission rate rose roughly 18-fold from toddlers (1.3%) to older adults (23.3%). Non-routine ED disposition increased with age, and syncope- or medical-related falls had the highest non-routine ED disposition rate (33.9%). The home was the most common injury setting (63.1%). Injury exposures varied by age group, with beds most common in infants, tables in toddlers, sports equipment in children and adolescents, and floors in older adults. Head, face, and neck injuries represent a large and growing share of NEISS-coded ED presentations, with distinct patterns by age, sex, injury mechanism, setting, and clinical outcome. These findings may assist in the planning of targeted prevention strategies and future research on risk stratification for vulnerable age groups and injury mechanisms.

articles.title: Intravenous ibuprofen versus ketorolac for acute low back pain in the emergency department: a triple-blind randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: Considering the frequency of recurrence in low back pain (LBP), there is no single medication group with promising efficacy in acute settings. Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) provide better pain relief with rather low complications. Since ketorolac has been relatively effective, we compared its safety and efficacy with ibuprofen as an alternative for pain relief in acute LBP. In this multi-centric triple-blind randomized clinical trial, we compared intravenous (IV) ibuprofen and ketorolac in patients with acute LBP presenting to the EDs of three university hospitals. Group 1 received IV ibuprofen (800 mg), and group 2 received IV ketorolac (30 mg), based on a computerized random sequence. Trained head nurses prepared analgesics in blocks of four. Neither patients nor the researcher or the statistician knew about the medication. We applied Visual Analog Scale (VAS) for patients to score their pain at baseline and 10 and 30 min after pain medications. Of 73 enrolled patients, 39 were in the ketorolac group and 34 participants in the ibuprofen group. Pain scores were significantly lower in the ibuprofen group at both 10 min (49.6 vs 57.4; p =0.013) and 30 min (32.2 vs 40.7; p =0.038). Based on the pain intensity after 30 min, the majority of patients in the ibuprofen group (70.6%) rated their pain as mild, while only 35.9% of the ketorolac group reported pain relief to a mild level (p <0.001). The mean ED length of stay was significantly lower in the ibuprofen group, whereas rescue analgesia and adverse events were comparable between the groups. Pain intensity was significantly lower in the ibuprofen group than in the ketorolac group after 10 and 30 min, without a significant difference in side effects. Intravenous ibuprofen can serve as an acceptable alternative and might be more effective than ketorolac in acute LBP in the ED.

articles.title: miR-4521 regulates keratinocyte function after burn injury by targeting GABARAPL2.
articles.journal: Journal of burn care & research : official publication of the American Burn Association
articles.abstract: Burn wound healing involves complex molecular events. This study sought to investigate the role of miR-4521 in burns by examining its expression in burned tissue and its regulation of keratinocyte function. Wound edge tissues from 116 burn patients and 102 normal skin samples were collected. miR-4521 expression was detected by qRT-PCR, followed by correlation analysis with clinical parameters and diagnostic evaluation. In vitro, cell viability was measured by CCK-8, inflammatory cytokines by ELISA, and oxidative stress markers by biochemical assays. The miR-4521 and GABARAPL2 interaction was validated through bioinformatic prediction combined with dual-luciferase and RIP assays. Expression of miR-4521 was markedly elevated in burn tissues compared to normal skin, with its levels positively correlating with burn surface area (r = 0.733), CRP (r = 0.661), and WBC count (r = 0.648). ROC curve analysis further suggested a diagnostic value for miR-4521 in burns, yielding an AUC of 0.849. In vitro, suppressing miR-4521 enhanced cell viability following heat injury while reducing inflammation, alongside alleviating oxidative stress. GABARAPL2, downregulated in burn tissues, was identified as a direct target of miR-4521 and inversely correlated with its expression (r = -0.704). In conclusion, The upregulation of miR-4521 in burn tissues showed close associations with both injury severity and inflammatory markers. By targeting GABARAPL2, miR-4521 inhibition attenuated heat-induced inflammation and oxidative stress in keratinocytes, positioning this microRNA as a possible therapeutic candidate for burn wound management.

articles.title: Association Between Early Bedside Clinical Findings and Need for Organ Support or Mortality in Critically Ill Children: A Multicenter Study.
authors: Critically Ill Patient Working Group of the Spanish Society of Pediatric Emergencies (SEUP)
articles.abstract: To identify early bedside clinical predictors of the need for organ support and mortality among critically ill children presenting to pediatric emergency departments (EDs). We conducted a prospective, registry-based, multicenter observational study across 21 pediatric emergency departments endorsed by the Spanish Society of Pediatric Emergencies. Critically ill children evaluated on the 4th, 14th, and 24th days of each month between February 2021 and July 2024 were included. Critical illness was defined as pediatric intensive care unit admission or advanced airway or circulatory intervention in the ED. The Pediatric Assessment Triangle (PAT) was recorded at arrival. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with severe clinical outcomes and mortality. Model discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). We included 412 critically ill children; 63 (15.3%) had severe clinical outcomes, and 12 (2.9%) died. Abnormal circulation and appearance when evaluating the PAT and abnormal systolic blood pressure were independently associated with severe clinical outcomes (AUC: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.68-0.82). Prior pediatric intensive care unit admission and abnormal appearance and abnormal circulation when evaluating the PAT were independently associated with mortality (AUC: 0.85; 95% CI: 0.76-0.95). Structured bedside assessment at ED presentation may provide clinically meaningful prognostic insight, supporting earlier prioritization and escalation of care for critically ill children, pending external validation.

articles.title: Evaluating Classifier Derivation and Validation Beyond the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve.
articles.abstract: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) summarizes a classifier's discrimination across all possible thresholds, but it does not establish calibration, clinical utility, or performance at the threshold used in practice. This editorial explains the interpretation and limitations of AUROC using a hypothetical genomic enzyme test for susceptibility to symptomatic COVID-19. It emphasizes that threshold selection must be justified according to the intended use, outcome prevalence, and consequences of false-positive and false-negative results. Threshold derivation and validation should be treated as separate processes, and performance should be evaluated in independent or appropriately internally validated data. Reporting should generally include sensitivity and specificity with 95% confidence intervals and the complete confusion matrix, from a validation dataset. AUROC P-values should receive limited emphasis; effect magnitude, precision, and decision-relevant performance are more informative.
keywords: Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve

articles.title: Low-Titer O + Whole Blood Implementation in the EMS System for Metropolitan Oklahoma City and Tulsa: Significance, Success, & Sharing Lessons Learned.
articles.abstract: Over 300 emergency medical services (EMS) organizations across the United States have implemented transfusion programs for traumatic injuries using packed red blood cells, platelets, plasma, or whole blood before hospital arrival. Beginning in December of 2022, the EMS System for Metropolitan Oklahoma City (OKC) and Tulsa began carrying low-titer O-positive whole blood (LTOWB) for adult patients in traumatic hemorrhagic shock, specifically those exhibiting elevated shock indexes. We aim to describe establishing our prehospital LTOWB program and its first two years of operations across OKC and Tulsa. We used an observational study design and retrospective descriptive analysis of patients receiving LTOWB by paramedic transfusion from the Emergency Medical Services Authority Ambulance Service, Oklahoma City Fire Department, or Tulsa Fire Department between December 1, 2022, and February 1, 2025. Descriptive analysis and univariate logistic regression quantify the relationship of patient characteristics against survival to hospital arrival and survival to hospital discharge outcomes. Penetrating trauma was the most common mechanism of injury recorded for patients receiving EMS LTOWB (71.6%). Following LTOWB transfusion, prehospital vital signs (systolic blood pressure, heart rate, and shock index) significantly improved (p < 0.05). Systolic blood pressure improvement conferred 9.7 times greater odds of survival to hospital arrival (95% CL 1.6-58.6). Occurrence of prehospital traumatic circulatory arrest was significantly related to lower odds of survival to hospital arrival and survival to hospital discharge (OR 1.01 and OR 1.04, respectively). Transfusion of LTOWB in a large, urban EMS system in the Southwestern United States confers a positive benefit to patients with measurable improvement in median systolic blood pressure, heart rate, and shock index. Continuous review of cases and misses empowered our system in dynamic protocol adjustments to best meet our population's needs. Patients often had secondary deterioration during transit, illustrating that blood transfusion "bought" temporary time during transport of critically injured patients to definitive care.

articles.title: Indicators of Surfers as Aquatic Rescuers in Coastal Environments in Brazil: Profile and Potential Based on Cluster Analysis.
articles.abstract: IntroductionDrowning is a major public health problem and ranks among the leading causes of death worldwide, especially in low- and middle-income countries. Surfers may play a relevant role as informal aquatic rescuers.ObjectiveTo assess the potential of surfers to act as aquatic rescuers by analyzing their knowledge of rescue and first aid in Brazilian coastal environments.MethodsThis cross-sectional study included 171 surfers over 18 years of age, of both sexes, recruited by convenience through an electronic questionnaire. Participants who self-reported autonomy to paddle beyond the breaking zone and catch waves without assistance were included. The instrument comprised sociodemographic data, surfing experience, risk perception, knowledge of sea conditions, first-aid training, and history of rescues. Cluster analysis using the K-means algorithm was employed to group participants based on variables related to experience, risk perception, and technical knowledge, identifying homogeneous profiles regarding their potential for rescue activities.ResultsTwo distinct clusters were identified. Cluster 1 showed lower experience, less formal qualification, and less previous involvement in rescues. Cluster 2 comprised older surfers (43 ± 9 years), with longer surfing experience, predominantly male (79%), advanced technical level, professional involvement with surfing, first-aid training, and a higher frequency of rescues performed (p < 0.05).ConclusionSurfers with greater experience, higher technical level, and first-aid training show greater potential to act as informal aquatic rescuers. A substantial proportion of participants lack formal training, underscoring the need for structured training strategies.

articles.title: Estimated plasma volume status (ePVS) as a prognostic marker in polytrauma: predicting 30-day mortality and coagulation support needs.
articles.abstract: Estimated plasma volume status (ePVS), derived from a simple formula based on haematocrit and haemoglobin values, has been associated with an unfavourable prognosis in many cardiovascular conditions, demonstrating a correlation with volume overload and the haemodynamic status of the patient. Indeed, ePVS was demonstrated to estimate the degree of congestion and was independently associated with cardiovascular outcomes, rehospitalization, and death in patients with heart failure (HF), confirming its prognostic value also in inflammatory pathologies. Due to its easy and immediate availability even in the emergency department (ED), ePVS may be useful in trauma patients to improve their initial evaluation and management. The aim of this retrospective observational study was to evaluate the role of ePVS at ED admission in predicting mortality and blood products use, red blood cells (RBC) and fresh frozen plasma (FFP), in trauma. We included 790 patients, of whom 67.7% were male; mean age 43.9 years; median Injury Severity Score (ISS) 7.5. The 30-day mortality rate was 2.8% (22/790). The median ePVS was significantly increased in deceased as compared to survivors (5.76; 4.79-8.36 versus 4.41; 3.92-5.05; p < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression analysis demonstrated that ePVS is an independent risk factor even after adjusting for other variables associated with 30-day mortality (odds radio, OR of 1.23; 95% confidence interval, CI 1.016-1.478, p = 0.034). Prediction of 30-day mortality for ePVS showed an AUROC of 0.776 (95% CI 0.666-0.887). Moreover, ePVS showed a positive correlation with the number of packed RBC and FFP units transfused, both during ED management, within the first 24 h, and over the entire hospital stay. The present findings suggest ePVS as a quick and easy tool to predict 30-day mortality and the need for blood resuscitation in trauma patients. Future studies may validate ePVS as a quick and easy tool for trauma victims' stratification and for predicting resource needs and mortality.

articles.title: Emergency surgery for blunt abdominal trauma in polytrauma - the impact of time to laparotomy on outcomes.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Blunt abdominal trauma (BAT) is common in polytrauma patients. Emergency surgery is required for haemodynamically significant solid organ injury and intra-abdominal hollow organ injury. The effect of time to surgery on outcomes in patients requiring emergency laparotomy remains uncertain. Adult polytrauma patients (ISS > 16) who underwent emergency laparotomy for blunt abdominal trauma between 1996 and 2020 from a trauma registry of a single level one trauma centre were included. Patients were divided into two groups based on the time elapsed from admission to emergency laparotomy: "Super Early" (≤ 60 min) and "Early" (60-180 min). Length of stay (LOS), intensive care unit (ICU)-LOS, ventilation time, re-look operations and mortality were assessed. Adjusted logistic regression was used to determine the independent predictive parameters, including timing of surgery, for mortality. The study included 190 polytrauma patients with concomitant blunt abdominal trauma (mean age 42 years (± 17), median ISS of 36 (IQR: 19)). There were 95 patients in each group. Patients in the "Super Early" group had a compromised haemodynamic status and a higher ISS. Liver injury and serous membrane injury were more common in the super early group. The mortality rate was significantly higher in the "Super Early" group (51.6%) compared to the "Early" group (26.3%) (p < 0.001). Death due to haemorrhagic shock was significantly more frequent in the "Super Early" group (36.8%) compared to the "Early" group (13.7%) (p < 0.001). A regression model was adjusted to determine the independent predictors of mortality. Time to emergency laparotomy was not an independent predictor of mortality. However, increased ISS (OR = 1.04, p = 0.049), age (OR = 1.03, p = 0.037) and decreased systolic blood pressure (OR = 0.98, p = 0.025) were found to be significant predictors of mortality. The timing of surgery showed no independent association with mortality as long as an emergency laparotomy was performed within 3 h of admission. The data suggests that patient-specific characteristics, injury severity and clinical status are more important for survival than the timing of an early emergency laparotomy. Future research should focus on determining the role of delayed laparotomy on outcomes in specific subgroups of patients.

articles.title: High-velocity trauma by social media: a new mechanism of injury in pediatric traumatology?
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Over the past two decades, social media challenges have emerged as a significant cause of injuries among adolescents. This study evaluates a sudden cluster of severe upper limb injuries resulting from the viral "Superman challenge" to raise clinical awareness of digital behaviors in pediatric trauma. A retrospective study at a tertiary pediatric trauma center evaluated patients aged < 18 years admitted in December 2024 following the "Superman challenge." Eight patients were admitted within a 10-day window following high-energy injuries from the challenge. The cohort showed a female predominance (62.5%) with a mean age of 13.25 (±1.03) years. The high-velocity mechanism led to atypical, severe injury patterns distinct from routine accidental falls. We observed an unusual cluster of severe distal forearm fractures in five patients, which uniformly required surgical treatment. Three patients even suffered bilateral distal radius fractures. Additional associated injuries included fractures of the ulnar styloid process (n = 5) and concomitant TFCC tears (n = 2), reflecting the high-energy nature of the challenge. The rapid, viral spread of physical social media challenges such as the 'Superman Challenge' can lead to dangerous injury mechanisms involving high-velocity trauma among children and adolescents. These trends could lead to sudden, localized clusters of atypical high-energy injuries-a scenario that, under specific conditions, risks overtaxing conventional healthcare systems, as previously demonstrated in the literature. Medical staff need to be aware of changing digital behaviors, which represent a new mechanism of injury in pediatric trauma.

articles.title: When Less Is More: Noninvasive Rewarming of a Severely Hypothermic Trauma Patient.
Surgical stabilization of rib fractures in a high-altitude trauma cohort: in-hospital clinical outcomes and resource use in a propensity score-weighted retrospective cohort study.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) is increasingly used in the management of traumatic rib fractures, but its in-hospital outcomes in high-altitude trauma settings remain uncertain. We evaluated the association of SSRF with in-hospital pulmonary complications and length of stay in a high-altitude (≈ 3,500 m) trauma system. We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of adults with CT-confirmed traumatic rib fractures admitted from 2015 to 2023 and managed with SSRF or non-operative management. Confounding was addressed using stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) with augmented outcome models; overlap weighting, propensity score matching, and time-dependent exposure analysis were used as sensitivity analyses. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital pneumonia, atelectasis, or respiratory failure. Pulmonary risk ratios (RRs) were estimated using modified Poisson regression, while ICU and hospital length of stay were analyzed using log-transformed weighted models. Among 324 patients, 121 underwent SSRF and 203 received non-operative management. Before adjustment, SSRF patients had greater injury severity. In IPTW-augmented analyses, the pulmonary estimate was imprecise (RR 0.86, 95% CI 0.23-3.21; P = 0.822), and no significant difference was detected in ICU length of stay (exp[β] 1.04, 95% CI 0.97-1.10; P = 0.286). Hospital length of stay was longer with SSRF (exp[β] 2.31, 95% CI 2.02-2.65; P < 0.001). Adjusted analyses found no statistically detectable difference in pulmonary complications or ICU length of stay, although the pulmonary estimate remained imprecise and does not establish equivalence or safety. SSRF was associated with longer hospital length of stay. Not applicable.

articles.title: A Drone-Integrated Artificial Intelligence-Based System for Mass-Casualty Triage and Remote Monitoring.
articles.abstract: Triage and data transfer are critical to the medical management of mass-casualty incidents (MCIs). However, the chaotic nature of such events makes it difficult to classify casualties according to structured triage protocols. Furthermore, even when triage is implemented effectively, communication disruptions between the incident scene and dispatch centers can hinder response operations. The aim of this study was to present a drone-integrated system that enables non-contact vital sign measurement, remote triage, and real-time data transmission during MCIs. The system development process involved three steps: (1) developing the Vital-Sign Measurement Module; (2) developing the Triage Decision Support Module; and (3) developing the User Interfaces and Data Transmission Module to enable information transmission between dispatch centers and response teams. Within the Vital-Sign Measurement Module, heart rate (HR), respiratory rate (RR), oxygen saturation (SpO2), and body temperature (BT) measurement algorithms were developed using the following techniques, respectively: video-based photoplethysmography (vPPG), analysis of thermal temperature fluctuations around the nose, a regression-based neural network approach, and heat maps and thermal thresholding. A pilot study was conducted under controlled indoor conditions to evaluate the accuracy of these algorithms. The system can measure vital signs by processing drone-captured images, can provide triage decision support, and can transmit victims' locations, vital signs, and triage categories to response teams and dispatch centers via dedicated user interfaces. A pilot evaluation of the Vital-Sign Measurement Module showed that the relative accuracy rate of the non-contact vital-sign measurement algorithms ranged from 86% to 99%. The system provides an innovative approach to improving medical response management in MCIs by enabling remote triage and monitoring. Its non-contact vital sign measurement, triage decision support, and near real-time data transmission capabilities provide an infrastructure that can contribute to faster response and improved operational coordination. However, further field trials and development are required to improve the robustness of the vital-sign measurement algorithms to motion, to improve their adaptability to changing environmental conditions, and to maintain high accuracy despite individual differences.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of high-sensitivity point-of-care troponin assays in emergency department for patients presenting with chest pain: a systematic review.
articles.journal: European journal of emergency medicine : official journal of the European Society for Emergency Medicine
articles.abstract: High-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn) assays have significantly enhanced the diagnosis in patients suspected of acute coronary syndrome (ACS). New hs-cTn point-of-care (POC) devices (turnaround time <20 min) may significantly reduce time to diagnosis. We evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of four currently commercially available hs-cTn POC devices to assess their potential for clinical implementation at the emergency department (ED). We conducted a search in PubMed Central on 20 November, 2025. Studies were included if they investigated patients greater than or equal to 18 years presenting with chest pain suggestive of ACS and evaluated commercially available hs-cTn POC devices. Studies had to report diagnostic accuracy [sensitivity, specificity, negative predictive value (NPV), positive predictive value] for the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Studies were assessed for risk of bias and applicability using the QUADAS-3 tool. We identified 436 articles. The 11 included studies consisted of both derivation and validation studies, including a total of 10 115 patients. The hs-cTn POC assays demonstrated the best diagnostic accuracy when applied as a single-test rule-out upon arrival at the ED, showing the following sensitivity and NPV: Atellica VTLi sensitivity 98.8-100% for troponin less than 4 ng/L (NPV: 99.8-100%) and 100% for troponin less than 7 ng/L (NPV 100%). Pathfast sensitivity 96.3-100% for troponin less than 3 ng/L (NPV: 98.1-100%). i-STAT sensitivity of 99.8% for troponin less than 5 ng/L (NPV: 100%). TriageTrue sensitivity of 100% for troponin less than 3 ng/L (NPV 100%). VTLi, Pathfast, and TriageTrue were also tested using the 99th percentile with a 0 + 1/2/3 h troponin protocol. Reported sensitivities: VTLi 64.8-100%, Pathfast 87% for plasma and 83% for whole blood, and TriageTrue 79.8%. Hs-cTn POC assays are reliable for integration into the diagnostic pathways for patients presenting with chest pain at the ED, mainly when used for rapid rule-out of AMI in patients with very low troponin values upon arrival.

articles.title: Human Factors-Driven Optimization of Pediatric Resuscitation Workflow Using Integrated Color-Coded Systems: A Randomized Crossover Study.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated whether a human factors-driven, integrated, color-coded resuscitation system that combines equipment standardization and prefilled-medication cognitive aids improves workflow efficiency and accuracy compared with a conventional crash cart during simulated pediatric resuscitations. A prospective, randomized, crossover simulation study was conducted with 28 health care professionals. Each team participated in 2 pediatric resuscitation scenarios using either the SCC or the CCCC in random order. All sessions were video-recorded to measure equipment retrieval and medication preparation times. Statistical comparisons were made using paired statistical tests appropriate for crossover designs, with significance set at P<0.05. Use of the CCCC significantly reduced the time to locate airway devices (13.1±6.9 vs. 41.7±22 s, P<0.001) and airway adjuncts (13.8±11.9 vs. 30.8±17.4 s, P=0.03). Prefilled color-coded syringes significantly reduced medication preparation time (median: 16 vs. 19 s; absolute reduction 3 s, P=0.04), with no dosing errors observed. Teams using the CCCC demonstrated more consistent workflow and fewer procedural delays. In this randomized crossover simulation study, the integrated color-coded system reduced equipment retrieval and medication preparation times for selected pediatric resuscitation tasks. These findings are limited to the simulation setting and should be interpreted in light of the Broselow framework's use for both cart organization and assessment of correct equipment selection. Further research is needed to evaluate the feasibility of color-coded prefilled syringes and determine whether the observed workflow benefits translate to real-world pediatric patient care.

articles.title: Association Between Childhood Opportunity Index and Pediatric Emergency Department Utilization of Youth With Experiences of Trafficking: A National Multicenter Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: To understand associations between the Child Opportunity Index (COI), a neighborhood-based measure of resources that influence child health and development, and pediatric ED utilization among youth with experiences of trafficking in the United States, as well as to describe their range of COI, sociodemographic characteristics, and pediatric ED utilization. This was a retrospective, observational, cohort study. We identified (by ICD-10 code) youth with experiences of trafficking who presented to pediatric EDs across 50 US children's hospitals between January 2018 and February 2023 within the Pediatric Health Information System database. Descriptive analyses and multivariate regression were performed. We identified 908 youth with experiences of trafficking who presented to pediatric EDs. Among them, 55% (n=499) were from neighborhoods with Very Low and Low COI, while 45% (n=409) were from neighborhoods with Moderate to Very High COI. Mental health diagnoses were common (n=584, 65.3%), and mental health, child abuse, and physical trauma were the top diagnosis categories for ED visits. Low-resource intensity visits were uncommon (12.8%). One-third of patients had an ED visit in the year prior. We did not find major statistically significant associations between COI and hospital utilization. In this cohort of youth with experiences of trafficking, all levels of COI and a wide range of visit acuity levels were represented. Further study is needed to better understand the prevalence and health needs of youth with experiences of trafficking who receive ED care, to develop effective screening and intervention programs to support these youth.

articles.title: Continuous Pulse Oximetry Analysis to Predict Outcomes in Young Infants With Bronchiolitis Presenting to the Emergency Department.
articles.abstract: Predictive analytics using continuously measured vital signs from bedside monitors has improved outcomes in critically ill children. We investigated whether continuous pulse oximetry data collected during emergency department (ED) evaluation can identify infants ≤90 days old with bronchiolitis at low risk of respiratory deterioration. We conducted a single-center retrospective cohort study of infants ≤90 days old with bronchiolitis who presented to a tertiary-care pediatric ED from November 2021 to November 2025. Infants were identified using the ICD-10 code with manual eligibility confirmation. Heart rate and oxygen saturation features were generated from continuous pulse oximetry during the first 2 hours of ED evaluation. The primary outcome was respiratory deterioration within 24 hours of ED arrival, defined as initiation of high-flow nasal cannula, continuous/bilevel positive airway pressure, or invasive mechanical ventilation. Data were split into derivation and validation cohorts (70/30, stratified by outcome). An L2-regularized logistic regression model estimated the probability of respiratory deterioration, with a classification threshold selected to prioritize sensitivity. Of 290 infants meeting clinical eligibility, 117 had sufficient continuous pulse oximetry data; 57 (49%) had respiratory deterioration. The primary model included 3 features: the median and interquartile range (IQR) of heart rate, and oxygen saturation IQR. In the validation cohort, the model showed moderate sensitivity (0.78, 95% CI: 0.58-0.95) and fair discrimination (AUROC=0.78, 95% CI: 0.62-0.93). We derived and validated a model using data from continuous pulse oximetry to identify low-risk infants with bronchiolitis. With further refinement and integration into monitor design systems, this approach may enhance clinical utility of continuous pulse oximetry.

articles.title: Factors Associated with Low-Acuity EMS Transport to the Emergency Department: An Observational Study Guided by the Andersen Behavioral Model.
articles.abstract: Emergency medical services (EMS) demand is increasing, with a growing proportion of low-acuity encounters. Prior studies are limited by regional sampling, inconsistent definitions, narrow observation periods, and limited theoretical grounding. The objective of this study was to identify predisposing, enabling, and need-based factors associated with EMS transport among low-acuity emergency department (ED) patients, guided by Andersen's Behavioral Model of Health Services Use. We conducted a secondary, retrospective observational study using a 10% random sample of multicenter electronic health record data from 21 EDs in the southeastern United States. Eligible visits included: (1) patient age >17 years, (2) occurred between January 1, 2016, and April 29, 2025, (3) triaged as Emergency Severity Index 4 or 5, and (4) ended in a final visit disposition of discharge. The primary outcome was arrival at the ED by EMS. We categorized independent variables as predisposing, enabling, or need-based factors according to Andersen's model. We used multivariable logistic regression to estimate adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Among 41,761 low-acuity ED encounters, 3,232 (7.7%) arrived by EMS. Higher odds of EMS use were observed for older age (per 10-year increase; aOR 1.33, 95% CI = 1.30-1.36), male sex (aOR 1.20, 95% CI = 1.12-1.30), being retired or disabled (aOR 3.60, 95% CI = 3.15-4.10), being unemployed (aOR 2.26, 95% CI = 2.04-2.52), having a nighttime presentation (aOR 1.63, 95% CI = 1.51-1.76), and mental health diagnosis (aOR 1.76, 95% CI = 1.62-1.90). Lower odds of EMS arrival were observed for white race (aOR 0.89, 95% CI = 0.83-0.96), established primary care (aOR 0.57, 95% CI = 0.53-0.62), weekend presentation (aOR 0.91; 95% CI = 0.84-0.99), and visits during (aOR 0.63, 95% CI = 0.55-0.71) or after (aOR 0.54, 95% CI = 0.48-0.61) the COVID-19 period. Rurality, insurance, and primary language were not associated with EMS use. Among low-acuity ED patients, EMS arrival was associated with older age, unemployment or disability, no established primary care clinician, and a previous mental health diagnosis. These characteristics identify a population that may be served by alternatives to ambulance transport, such as treat-in-place and alternative destination pathways, when paired with expanded access to primary care and behavioral health resources.

articles.title: Missed Opportunities for Prehospital Transfusion in Pediatric Trauma.
articles.abstract: Prehospital blood transfusion has been associated with improved outcomes among pediatric trauma patients, but its utilization nationally remains poorly understood. We recently conducted a similar study that builds upon the findings of the investigation by Ramgopal et al. to identify potential missed opportunities for prehospital transfusion in pediatric trauma. We utilized the National EMS Information System dataset from 2018-2023 to identify emergency medical services (EMS) responses for pediatric (<18 years of age) trauma patients. We identified trauma patients using the CDC Injury Mortality Diagnosis Matrix related ICD-10 codes. We identified patients at increased risk of benefiting from a transfusion using age-adjusted positive shock index thresholds. The outcome of interested was prehospital blood or blood product transfusion. We found there were 1,663,601 total 9-1-1 EMS activations to a scene for pediatric trauma. There were 363,844 patients with a positive shock index who were considered to be at increased risk of benefiting from a prehospital transfusion, but only 287 (0.1%) of these patients received a prehospital transfusion. Only 10 (2%) of the 468 patients who experienced a cardiac arrest after the arrival of EMS to the scene received a hospital transfusion. Together, our results indicate prehospital transfusion rates ranging from 0.1% to 1.01% among potentially eligible pediatric trauma patients. Although positive shock index does not confirm hemorrhagic shock, these findings suggest underutilization of prehospital blood transfusion among pediatric trauma patients.

articles.title: Personalized Remote Patient Management in Heart Failure : From Implanted Hemodynamic Monitoring Toward an Artificial Intelligence-Supported Adaptive Care Cycle.
articles.abstract: Implanted pulmonary artery pressure (PAP) monitoring provides an early window on imminent worsening heart failure (HF). Randomized trials demonstrated that PAP-guided management significantly reduces HF hospitalizations, but substantial residual risk persists despite recent major advances in HF pharmacotherapy. We review lessons from PAP-guided remote patient management and examine how artificial intelligence (AI) could support more individualized eligibility assessment and multimodal longitudinal surveillance within a patient-centered adaptive care cycle to further improve clinical outcomes. HF is increasingly recognized as a systemic disease characterized, across HF phenotypes, by multiple cardiac and non-cardiac comorbidities. CHAMPION, GUIDE-HF, and MONITOR-HF did not systematically incorporate comorbidity-related risk into patient selection, while PAP-guided treatment focused predominantly on diuretic adjustment, and monitoring strategies were not adapted to individual disease trajectories. AI could help integrate multidimensional phenotyping to estimate individual risk and expected benefit pre-implant, use comprehensive longitudinal monitoring data to support personalized, actionable clinical decision-making, and enable dynamic adaptation of monitoring intensity tailored to the disease trajectory. This may improve clinical outcomes, reduce healthcare professional workload, enhance patient experience and treatment adherence, and increase cost-effectiveness.

articles.title: Using a Single Dose of Dexamethasone at 0.6 Versus 0.15 mg/kg of Body Weight for the Treatment of Croup: A Multicenter Retrospective Chart Review.
articles.abstract: To compare the effectiveness and adverse events associated with treating children with croup with dexamethasone at 0.15 versus 0.6 mg/kg body weight. This retrospective cohort study included children (younger than 18 y) with a clinical diagnosis of croup in 4 pediatric emergency departments (EDs) between January 2017 and December 2019. The primary outcome was return visit to the ED for croup within 7 days, and the secondary outcomes were hospitalization within 7 days and occurrence of adverse events within 30 days. Both χ2 tests and logistic regression models were used to compare differences in the proportions of children with ED return visits, hospitalizations, and adverse events associated with dose. We included 14,205 children in the final analysis. Of the 13,437 croup episodes from children treated with dexamethasone at 0.15 mg/kg (n=172) or 0.6 mg/kg (n=13,265), 2.9% and 4.1%, respectively, were ED return visits within 7 days following treatment. The difference in the proportion of ED return visits following treatment with the 2 doses was not statistically significant (1.2%; 95% CI: -1.31 to 3.76). In a multivariable-adjusted model, 0.15 mg/kg was not associated with ED return visits within 7 days [adjusted odds ratio (aOR)=0.88; 95% CI: 0.31-1.97], but was associated with hospitalization (aOR=3.18; 95% CI: 1.52-6.00). A total of 135 (1%) of all croup episodes had at least 1 adverse event within 30 days. Of those treated with 0.15 or 0.6 mg/kg, 1.2% and 1%, respectively, had at least 1 adverse event within 30 days. The most common adverse event was pneumonia (0.8%). Our findings suggest that low-dose dexamethasone, 0.15 mg/kg, may be as effective as 0.6 mg/kg with comparable proportions of ED return visits and adverse events within 7 days. However, low-dose dexamethasone was associated with increased hospitalization. Clinicians should weigh the potential risk of hospitalization when choosing 0.15 mg/kg of dexamethasone.

articles.title: The role of low muscle strength in predicting mortality in patients with liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.
articles.abstract: Sarcopenia is a prevalent complication in chronic liver disease (CLD), traditionally assessed by muscle mass. Recent paradigm shifts focus to dynapenia as the primary determinant of adverse outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the role of dynapenia, as measured by handgrip strength (HGS) and ultrasound-derived diaphragmatic excursion, in predicting mortality in this population. This prospective study included consecutive outpatients with cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma history attending a tertiary hepatology unit. Muscle mass was assessed in subgroups using bioimpedance analysis (BIA) and computed tomography (CT). Associations between sarcopenia proxies and 24-month all-cause mortality were analyzed with adjusted Cox regression models, and survival was estimated using Kaplan-Meier curves. Ninety-one patients were included (age 73.4 ± 8.1 years; 71 [78%] male); 20 (22%) had dynapenia. Twenty-two deaths occurred at two years (24.2%). Over 24 months, dynapenia (by HGS) and diaphragmatic excursion were associated with mortality in adjusted models (aHR 1.68, 95% CI 1.12-2.53, p = 0.012; aHR 0.58, 95% CI 0.34-0.97, p = 0.042). In subgroups, they remained the only muscle parameters associated with mortality, while muscle mass indices were not significant. Finally, Kaplan-Meier estimates showed lower 24-month survival in dynapenic patients across groups (in overall population 65% vs. 79%, p = 0.05). Low muscle strength is a key prognostic parameter in patients with cirrhosis and HCC. In our small cohort, it was the only muscle-related measure significantly associated with mortality. These findings support further evaluation of muscle strength assessment as a potential tool for risk stratification in this population.

articles.title: Decreasing response phase lights and siren use through modification of dispatch priority response for 9-1-1 responses to personal emergency response system activations: an interventional study.
articles.abstract: Emergency medical services (EMS) responses to personal emergency response systems (PERS) activations predominantly involve low-acuity patients. Recent evidence demonstrates that while most PERS calls are dispatched lights and siren (L&S), only 1% result in L&S transport. Reduction of L&S use through modified dispatch priority response for PERS calls has not been evaluated. Our objective was to evaluate the efficacy of modifying dispatch priority response mode for PERS calls to non-L&S response, the resulting reduction in response phase L&S use, and potential impact on time critical interventions. We conducted a retrospective observational pre-post analysis comparing PERS responses in two 11-month periods before (January-November 2023) and after (January-November 2024) revising the dispatch priority response for PERS calls to non-L&S in December 2023. We evaluated response mode and transport mode. The primary outcome was total hours/month of response phase L&S use, with L&S duration computed as the interval between unit dispatched and arrival (patient contact) or call cancellation. Descriptive statistics were computed followed by interrupted time series analysis (ITSA) to assess the impact of the intervention on the primary outcome and maintenance of the effect across the post-intervention period (p for post-intervention linear trend). Analysis included 3,262 PERS calls (pre-intervention = 1,634; post-intervention = 1,628). L&S response occurred in 98% (n = 1,601) of pre-intervention calls and 12% (n = 192) of post-intervention calls (p < 0.001). The prevalence of L&S transport was similar in both periods (0.9% vs 0.9%, p = 0.99). The ITSA revealed an immediate 13.8-hour/month decrease in response phase L&S use (95% confidence interval: -16.2 to -11.3) that was sustained across the post-intervention period (p > 0.05). Total response phase L&S hours decreased 86%, from 172 hours in the pre-intervention period to 24 hours during the post-intervention period. Importantly, only four post-intervention calls (0.2%) involved a non-L&S response followed by L&S transport, with just one of these requiring advanced life support interventions. Modifying dispatch priority response for PERS calls reduced L&S responses and yielded a marked decrease in hours of L&S use which was maintained overtime. As the industry advocates for safer, more judicious L&S use, additional low-acuity call types should be identified for similar dispatch priority response revision.

articles.title: Prehospital Risk Stratification for Early Transfusion in Pediatric Trauma: A National Trauma Data Bank Analysis.
articles.abstract: Pediatric criteria remain limited for identifying injured children who may benefit from early blood transfusion for hemorrhagic shock. This study evaluated whether emergency medical services (EMS)-observable variables in a national trauma registry could identify children at risk for early hospital blood transfusion. We conducted an observational retrospective cohort study using the National Trauma Data Bank (2017-2020). Among 391,126 records for patients aged 1-15 years, we included children transported by EMS directly from the scene to a participating trauma center after excluding burn injuries, interfacility transfers, and missing pre-identified EMS variables (systolic blood pressure, heart rate, or Glasgow Coma Scale [GCS]). The primary outcome was any blood product administered within 4 hours of emergency department arrival. Five prespecified EMS-observable predictors composed the model: age-adjusted hypotension, age-adjusted tachycardia, GCS ≤14, penetrating mechanism, and prehospital traumatic cardiac arrest. We fit a multivariable logistic regression and a classification and regression tree (CART) using an 80/20 stratified train-validation split. Missing data sensitivity analyses included multiple imputation and CART refitting in the broader eligible cohort. Among 79,764 children, 2,634 (3.3%) received early transfusion in the hospital. All five predictors were independently associated with early transfusion, led by GCS ≤14 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 8.38; 95% confidence interval [CI], 7.61-9.22), penetrating mechanism (aOR 5.87; 95% CI, 5.28-6.51), and age-adjusted hypotension (aOR 5.39; 95% CI, 4.74-6.13). In the validation cohort, CART analysis stratified patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk tiers comprising 77.0%, 19.7%, and 3.3% of patients, respectively. Early-transfusion rates were 1.2%, 6.1%, and 36.7% across these tiers. The high-risk tier accounted for 36.8% of all early transfusion events. Using the high-risk tier as a decision threshold, sensitivity was 36.8%, specificity 97.8%, positive predictive value 36.7%, and negative predictive value 97.8%. Five EMS-observable features, including age-adjusted hypotension, age-adjusted tachycardia, GCS ≤14, penetrating mechanism, and prehospital traumatic cardiac arrest, identified a small subgroup of pediatric trauma patients with substantially elevated risk of early hospital transfusion. This parsimonious framework may inform prospective validation of prehospital transfusion criteria.

articles.title: Fasting before elective abdominal ultrasound: a systematic review and meta-analysis-comment.

Trends and Disparities in Pediatric Ophthalmologic Emergency Department Visits in New Jersey, 2020-2024: A 5-Year Population-Based Analysis.
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the volume, trends, and demographic disparities in pediatric ophthalmologic emergency department (ED) visits in New Jersey (NJ) from 2020 to 2024. This retrospective cross-sectional study used aggregate data from the NJ State Health Assessment Data (NJSHAD). We identified ED encounters among patients aged 0 to 19 years with primary ophthalmic ICD-10-CM diagnoses (H10, H00-H01, S05, H57.1, and T15). Temporal patterns were assessed using Pearson correlation and linear regression, with 2016 to 2019 used as a prepandemic reference. Demographic, payer, racial/ethnic rate, county, and workforce analyses were restricted to the 2020 to 2024 period. A total of 88,271 ophthalmologic ED encounters were included from 2016 to 2024. Annual volume averaged 12,095 encounters during 2016 to 2019 and fell to 4607 in 2020, 61.9% below the prepandemic mean. Visits subsequently recovered, although 2024 volume remained 15.2% below the 2016 to 2019 mean. Conjunctivitis remained near 30% of its prepandemic mean in 2020 to 2021, while traumatic diagnoses recovered from 51.4% to 71.0%. During 2020 to 2024, 39,890 encounters accounted for 1.37% of pediatric ED visits; Medicaid was the primary payer in 52.1% of cases. Conjunctivitis visit rates were 7.78 times higher among Black non-Hispanic children and 5.13 times higher among Hispanic children than among White non-Hispanic children. County rates correlated with Medicaid enrollment (r=0.861, P<0.001). Pediatric ophthalmologic ED visits in NJ fell sharply during the COVID-19 pandemic and subsequently recovered toward prepandemic levels. Higher conjunctivitis encounter rates among Black non-Hispanic and Hispanic children and in counties with greater Medicaid enrollment suggest persistent disparities in access to outpatient eye care.

articles.title: Circadian and Seasonal Patterns of Recorded Emergency Medical Service Workload by Diagnostic Category: A Two-Year Retrospective Analysis with Forecasting from Türkiye.
articles.abstract: Emergency Medical Services (EMS) demand varies across circadian, weekly, and seasonal timescales. This study is among the first such integrated analyses in the Turkish 112 EMS context. The primary objective of this study was to characterize circadian patterns in overall EMS case-record volume and across seven clinical groups, as well as hourly, weekly, and seasonal variation in diagnostic composition across eight categories. Secondary objectives were to estimate adjusted temporal associations and evaluate frozen transfer of aggregate daily forecasts from 2024 to the immediately subsequent 2025 holdout. This retrospective study analyzed 60,811 routinely collected EMS case-record rows from Karaman Province, Türkiye over 731 days in 2024-2025. Interaction, cosinor, and negative binomial (NB) models characterized temporal patterns; aggregate daily case-record volume was forecast using weekly Fourier terms with autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) errors trained on 2024 and frozen for 2025. The data represented provincial case-record workload, an operational proxy for population demand rather than a census of all inbound calls or unique patients. Case-record volume peaked at 21:00 and was lowest at 06:00; adjusted volume at 21:00 was 3.53-times that at 06:00 (95% CI, 3.28-3.81). Hourly diagnostic composition differed modestly (Cramér V = 0.061). Rhythmicity was detected in all seven clinical groups (all joint-test P values < 0.001), but low full-cell R2 values indicated substantial unexplained hour-date variation; acrophases ranged from 14:41 to 19:14 and relative amplitudes from 28.6% (Respiratory) to 67.9% (Trauma). Standardized Trauma share was higher in summer than winter (25.7% versus 18.1%), whereas Respiratory share was higher in winter than summer (9.7% versus 3.6%). Adjusted volume was higher on Monday than Saturday and higher in August than November (IRRs 1.11 and 1.23, respectively). In the frozen 2025 holdout, the selected model achieved mean absolute scaled error (MASE) = 0.722 and 95% prediction-interval coverage of 96.2%. Clinical-group rhythms and seasonal composition differences were observed. The frozen evaluation quantified aggregate daily forecast transfer only from 2024 to the immediately subsequent 2025 within one provincial series. Findings support local monitoring of recorded evening workload and seasonal diagnostic composition, particularly the higher Trauma share in summer and the higher Respiratory share in winter.

articles.title: Recurrent cardiac tamponade in a young man unmasking an endocrine surprise: a case record.
Penetrating renal trauma in a high-complexity Latin American centre: Management patterns and renal preservation, 2013-2025 - a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Contemporary renal-trauma practice rests on blunt-predominant cohorts from high-income trauma systems, and penetrating renal injury remains under-described. We characterised the management and outcomes of penetrating renal trauma at a high-complexity Latin American centre, with blunt injury as internal comparator, and examined how practice changed over 13 years. Retrospective cohort of 161 consecutive adults (≥18 years) treated between February 2013 and July 2025, classified by mechanism. Management, nephrectomy and in-hospital outcomes are reported descriptively as n (%) and median [IQR]. Testing was confined to three pre-specified questions: whether nephrectomy differed by mechanism; whether it differed by mechanism among patients taken to open surgery; and whether it changed over time. Two-sided exact p values were obtained by doubling the one-sided probability. Thirty-four injuries (21%) were penetrating (27 gunshot, 6 stab, 1 unspecified) and 126 (78%) blunt. Among penetrating injuries, 13 (38%) were managed non-operatively, 3 (9%) with angioembolisation and 18 (53%) with open surgery. Non-operative management was used up to AAST grade IV and failed in none, with no reintervention, nephrectomy or renal complication; angioembolisation preserved every treated kidney. Twelve of the 34 penetrating injuries (35%) ended in nephrectomy versus 5 of 126 blunt (4%; p < 0.001), and every nephrectomy in the cohort followed open surgery. Among the patients taken to open surgery, however, nephrectomy was equally frequent in the two groups (12 of 18 vs 5 of 9; p = 0.88), so renal loss tracked the decision to operate rather than intraoperative salvageability. High-grade (AAST IV-V) injury was similarly frequent by mechanism (41% vs 29%). Within penetrating injuries, open surgery fell from 15 of 24 in 2013-2019-3 of 10 in 2020-2025, and nephrectomy from 11 of 24-1 of 10, with a stable mechanism mix. Selective non-operative management and angioembolisation preserved every kidney in which they were used, including after penetrating injury, and renal loss followed the decision to operate rather than the mechanism itself. These data support extending physiology-guided, kidney-preserving management to penetrating renal injury.

articles.title: Work productivity and psychological well-being in patients affected by type 1 diabetes mellitus.
articles.abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1D) is a lifelong autoimmune condition that, when diagnosed during childhood or adolescence, may influence educational attainment, employment trajectories, and occupational functioning in adulthood. This observational cross-sectional study, conducted between June and September 2024 at the "Federico II" University Hospital in Naples, Italy, assessed work ability, work productivity, activity impairment, and psychological well-being in 70 adults with T1D. Sociodemographic, clinical, and occupational data were collected through structured interviews and medical record review. Work ability was evaluated using the Work Ability Index (WAI), productivity and activity impairment using the Work Productivity and Activity Impairment questionnaire (WPAI), and psychological well-being using the Psychological General Well-Being Index (PGWBI). Overall, 49% of participants were unemployed. Among employed individuals, work ability was generally preserved, with 72% reporting good or excellent WAI scores, although WAI declined significantly with age (p = 0.040). WPAI results showed low absenteeism (5.5%) but relevant presenteeism (26.7%) and activity impairment (42.7%). Activity impairment was higher among unemployed than employed participants (61.2% vs. 25.3%; p < 0.0001). Mean PGWBI scores indicated preserved psychological well-being (66.8 ± 20.3) but declined with increasing age (p = 0.001) and unemployment (p = 0.003). Higher PGWBI scores correlated with greater work ability (rs = 0.72, p < 0.0001) and lower activity impairment (rs = -0.79, p < 0.0001). Glycated hemoglobin, body mass index, occupational category, and insulin delivery technology were not significantly associated with outcomes. Overall, age and employment status emerged as relevant correlates of functional and psychological outcomes. These findings support integrated occupational strategies beyond glycemic control and appropriate targeted workplace accommodations.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Modified Masquelet technique using free vascularized fibula grafting for reconstruction of large bone defects after bone infection" [Injury 57(3) (2026) 113036].
Altered cholangiocyte subsets with neural pathway enrichment in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
articles.abstract: Hepatocytes have been extensively studied in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), yet the role of cholangiocytes remains underexplored. We utilized a comprehensive approach that integrates high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA), cellular interaction evaluation, machine learning techniques, immune cell infiltration analysis, and Mendelian randomization to investigate both single-cell sequencing data and bulk sequencing datasets. Single-cell analysis identified significant alterations in cholangiocyte subpopulations in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) patients, including an increase in cholangiocytes with elevated SEMA3 pathway expression. The hdWGCNA analysis identified the green module, which is enriched with genes associated with neural pathways pertinent to MASH. Seven machine learning models assessed the diagnostic feasibility of key genes in the green module for MASLD spectrum. Immune infiltration analysis highlighted complex interactions between cholangiocytes enriched for neural-related pathways and immune cells, particularly neutrophils and monocytes. Patient stratification identified two distinct subtypes within the MASLD spectrum, with subtype 2 exhibiting enhanced activity in neural-related pathways. Mendelian randomization analysis identified PLEKHA5 as a candidate causal gene for MASLD, suggesting a potential role in neural mechanisms (SEL1L3 showed a suggestive association, P = 0.0413). Collectively, this hypothesis-generating bioinformatics study elucidates distinct characteristics of cholangiocyte subpopulations in MASH, revealing neural pathway alterations that may contribute to disease pathogenesis and providing a foundation for future investigation into cholangiocyte-related mechanisms in MASLD.

articles.title: Comparison of low volume versus high-volume polyethylene glycol-based bowel preparation for colonoscopy in people receiving haemodialysis: a randomized non-inferiority trial.
articles.abstract: Colonoscopy in chronic kidney disease patients undergoing haemodialysis is crucial. Some concerns have been raised about the use of oral bowel cleansing agents for colonoscopy. We compared the efficacy, safety and tolerability of a low volume versus a high-volume polyethylene glycol-based bowel preparation for colonoscopy in such patients. A multicentre, parallel-arm, randomized, phase IV trial with 15% non-inferiority margin was conducted. Eligible subjects were allocated to either the low volume (2 L) or high-volume (4 L) bowel preparation group in 1:1 ratio. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants with adequate bowel cleansing. Secondary outcomes were polyp/adenoma detection rate (PDR/ADR), cecal intubation rate, patient tolerability/compliance and adverse events. Sixty-nine patients were randomized in four centres, 35 to low and 34 to high-volume groups. No difference in caecal intubation rate, in patients with adequate preparation, was observed (96.7% vs 100%, p = 1). As per-protocol, adequate bowel preparation was achieved in the 69.7 and 63.0% of low and high-volume groups, respectively (p = 0.58). The mean Boston Bowel Preparation Scale was similar in the two groups (5.6 ± 2.4vs 5.4 ± 2.4, p = 0.51). The PDR was 39.4% in low volume and 37.0% in high volume (p = 1). No differences in adverse events were observed. No emergency dialysis sessions were required. Serum creatinine levels remained stable before and after preparation in both groups. Optimal cleansing was difficult to obtain in haemodialysis patients. Both low and high-volume preparations were equally effective and safe. The small sample size is a limit underpowering our research. Larger studies are, therefore, required. Trial registration number The trial was approved by the Central ethic committee (protocol approval no. 0089971/23/11/2020) and registered on ClinicalTrials.gov NCT04709770.

articles.title: Pelvic hemorrhage in the context of demographic change: frequency and CT-based characterization of pelvic bleeding.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Traumatic pelvic hemorrhage is a major driver of morbidity and mortality in pelvic fractures. Classic literature described pelvic hemorrhage as predominantly venous, whereas arterial injury is considered less common. We evaluated the frequency, anatomical distribution, and presumed sources of pelvic hemorrhage in a contemporary trauma cohort using contrast-enhanced CT (CECT). We conducted a single-center, retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients with pelvic fractures treated at a level-I trauma center between 2020 and 2022. All patients underwent CECT at initial presentation. Two experienced pelvic trauma surgeons independently reviewed all scans. Radiologically relevant hemorrhage was defined by contrast extravasation, soft-tissue asymmetry/displacement, or a contained intrapelvic hematoma. Patients with and without hemorrhage were compared regarding age, sex, trauma mechanism, anticoagulation, and fracture type. The presumed bleeding sources were categorized as arterial, venous, cancellous, or mixed. Radiologically relevant hemorrhage occurred in 95/512 (18.6%) patients and was more frequent after high-energy trauma and in men. Iliac sites predominated, whereas presacral bleeding was uncommon. The presumed bleeding source was cancellous in 44.2%, mixed in 29.5%, arterial in 18.9%, and isolated venous in 7.4%. Overall mortality was 7.0% and was significantly higher in patients with hemorrhage (14.7% vs. 5.3%; p < 0.001). In this contemporary CECT-based cohort, pelvic hemorrhage was less frequent than historically reported, with CT findings most commonly suggesting cancellous or mixed bleeding sources. These findings suggest that the traditional concept of predominantly venous pelvic hemorrhage may not fully reflect current CT-based observations.

articles.title: The new trochanteric nail TFN-A has a higher complication rate in the treatment of proximal femoral fractures than the predecessor model PFN-A.
articles.journal: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
articles.abstract: Trochanteric fractures (TF) are among the most frequent fractures and have major impact on the affected patients and the healthcare system. Cephalomedullary nails (CMN) are widely used for these fractures. Complications remain frequent, either due to comorbidities or concerning the implant. The goal of this retrospective, single-centre study was to compare the complication rates of two CMN from one manufacturer. All internal fixations TF performed between 01/2017 and 07/2021 in our institution were analysed retrospectively. Follow-up was at least two years. The CMN were the PFN-A or the TFN-A. Demographic data, all reoperations and revisions were recorded. Reoperations and revisions were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method, with subgrouping as minor reoperation, minor revision or major revision, including conversion to total hip arthroplasty. A total of 492 CMN, used in 475 patients, could be included. Among these, 248 were PFN-A and 244 were TFN-A. The overall reoperation rate was 15%, 12.9% for the PFN-A and 17.2% for the TFN-A, respectively. The TFN-A group had significantly more major revisions (hazard ratio 3.57 (95% confidence interval 1.42-9.94; p = 0.004). No relevant differences were found regarding demographic data or the quality of reduction and internal fixation. The TFN-A had a significantly higher rate of complications leading to major revision than the former PFN-A. This may have been missed when considering only the reoperation rate for all causes due to a camouflage effect by minor complications.

articles.title: Wilderness & Environmental Medicine: The Year in Review.
Silent Hypoxemia in High-Altitude Pulmonary Edema: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: We report a case of a trekker who ascended to Tilicho Lake (4919 m) from Kathmandu (1400 m) in 3 days. On day 3, he descended to Shree Kharka (4045 m). The following day, he trekked to Yak Kharka (4025 m) where, although he had no symptoms, he measured his own oxygen saturation (SpO2) at 72% in ambient air. Overnight, his SpO2 ranged from 75-80% on oxygen 2L/min via nasal cannula. The next day his SpO2 dropped to 47% while still on oxygen. He descended on horseback to Manang (3500 m), where his SpO2 was 70% on room air. He was diagnosed with high-altitude pulmonary edema (HAPE). He was treated with oxygen, 4L by nasal cannula, and nifedipine. The following day, he flew to Kathmandu, where he made a full recovery. Trekkers may develop life-threatening HAPE without obvious symptoms or signs. Slow ascent can decrease the likelihood of developing HAPE, but trekkers do not always follow the recommended ascent rate. Early detection, by history and physical examination and with point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS), if available, is critical in resource-limited regions such as ours. The keys to managing HAPE are early recognition and management, including descending to a lower altitude as soon as possible.

articles.title: Essentials of Pediatric Emergency Medicine Fellowship: Clinical Updates From the Past Decade.
articles.abstract: Ten years ago, a comprehensive series of articles was published in Pediatric Emergency Care detailing the state of pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) fellowship education. We intend to provide an update to the clinical elements of fellowship training, with a companion article to follow that will address the nonclinical domains. This article will summarize the core components of fellowship as mandated by the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) and review significant changes and challenges to fellowship education that have occurred over the past decade. In light of upcoming modifications to fellowship education, including an increased focus on competency-based medical education and the addition of a 2-year, clinically oriented fellowship option, it is vital for stakeholders to be familiar with the core elements of PEM fellowship training as the curriculum is adapted to meet the needs of trainees and their patients.

articles.title: Evaluating Creative Cognition as a Risk and Resilience Factor for Burnout in Pediatric Emergency Medicine.
articles.abstract: Burnout is common among pediatric emergency medicine (PEM) physicians, but the relationship between creative problem-solving (CPS) preferences and burnout is not well understood. This study examined associations between CPS mindsets and burnout in PEM. This cross-sectional study included PEM (attending physicians and fellows) from 3 emergency departments. Measures: Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey for Burnout; FourSight for CPS preferences (clarifying, ideating, developing, implementing). The primary outcome was the association between burnout and CPS preferences, and the secondary outcomes were comparisons of burnout prevalence and CPS preferences in PEM compared with published norms. Participation was 100%, with 96.7% providing complete data. Participants: female 58%; median age 41 years; 51% White, 23% Asian, and 83% married. High clarifying scores were associated with greater emotional exhaustion (EE; adjusted β = 0.67; 95% CI, 0.15 to 1.19), with a stronger association among women (adjusted β = 0.76; 95% CI, 0.03 to 1.48). Ideating was associated with higher personal accomplishment (PA; β = 0.31; 95% CI, 0.08 to 0.55). In univariate analysis, female sex (β = 5.03; 95% CI, 0.17 to 9.89) and educational debt (β = 5.46; 95% CI, 0.47 to 10.4) were each associated with higher EE. Compared with health care norms, PEM demonstrated higher PA scores (mean = 5.00; 95% CI, 4.84 to 5.15 vs. 4.30). PEM were more likely to show an implementing mindset (55% vs. 21%, P < 0.001) and less likely to show a Developing mindset (10% vs. 23%, P = 0.007). A clarifying mindset was associated with higher EE, particularly among women, while Ideating was associated with greater PA. CPS self-awareness and targeted training may offer novel strategies to mitigate burnout among PEM.

articles.title: Equity-Related Factors in Emergency Medical Service Use for Acute Coronary Syndromes: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Emergency medical service (EMS) use reduces time to treatment and improves outcomes in acute coronary syndrome (ACS), yet it is unknown whether all Australians have equitable access to EMS. This systematic review examined whether equity-related factors are associated with disparities in EMS use for patients with ACS in Australia. The review was pre-registered with PROSPERO (CRD42023466951). Six databases (MEDLINE, CINAHL, Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Cochrane and Scopus) were searched in June 2025 for articles published from inception until May 2025. Eligible studies involved adults presenting to Australian hospitals or emergency departments with ACS or acute non-traumatic chest pain and reported EMS use by at least one PROGRESS-Plus equity-related factor. Risk of bias was assessed using JBI checklists. Findings were synthesized using tabular analysis and a vote-counting summary. Fourteen studies were identified, with twelve rated high quality. EMS utilization ranged from 36% to 79% and increased over time. Disparities were evident across multiple equity-related factors. Adults aged under 49 years had up to 68% lower odds of EMS use than those 65 years or older. Men had up to 11% lower odds than women. People born outside Australia had up to 15% lower odds, and those preferring non-English languages had 6-20% lower odds. Residents of remote areas had up to 25% lower odds than major city residents, while individuals living alone had up to 48% higher odds than those living with others. Findings for socioeconomic status measures were mixed. EMS use for ACS in Australia is consistently lower among younger adults, men, people born overseas, those preferring non-English languages, and residents of remote areas. These findings can inform targeted interventions to improve EMS accessibility. Future research should examine the mechanisms underlying these access barriers, particularly for populations experiencing multiple forms of disadvantage.

articles.title: Alcohol-positive polytrauma patients: injury patterns, ICU resource use and mortality at a German Level I trauma center.
articles.abstract: In most countries, alcohol consumption is so culturally ingrained that even small amounts are permitted while driving. Even at a blood alcohol concentration of 0.5 g/L, ethanol impairs mental and cognitive performance. Studies from the US and Europe estimate that elevated blood alcohol levels may be detected in 10%-40% of all emergency department patients. Against this background, we investigated the impact of alcohol consumption on injury severity, injury patterns, as well as primary and secondary outcomes in polytrauma patients. This retrospective, single-center cohort study included patients admitted to a Level I trauma center via the trauma room and documented in the TraumaRegister DGU® between 2015 and 2023. Serum ethanol was determined routinely in all adolescent and adult trauma room patients. Patients without serum ethanol measurement or younger than 13 years were excluded. Patients with detectable serum ethanol (> 1 mg/dL, detection limit of the laboratory; ALC) were compared with patients without (noALC) using the χ² and Mann-Whitney U tests. Multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses were adjusted for age, sex, Injury Severity Score (ISS), severe traumatic brain injury (TBI) and pre-injury ASA classification. A dose-response analysis was performed using serum ethanol categories. A total of 1,524 patients were analyzed: 431 (28.3%) were alcohol-positive (ALC) and 1,093 (71.7%) were not (noALC). ALC patients were younger, more often male and had a lower prehospital Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score (p < 0.001), whereas the ISS did not differ (p = 0.396). They were more frequently victims of violent crime and were overrepresented among pedestrians and falls from < 3 m, whereas motorcyclists were more often sober. Alcohol-positive patients were more often treated in the ICU (90.0% vs. 86.3%; p = 0.048), but this association was attenuated after multivariable adjustment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.40; 95% CI 0.96-2.03). Length of ICU stay and duration of mechanical ventilation did not differ, and alcohol was not independently associated with mortality (aOR 0.91; 95% CI 0.56-1.47). Severe TBI was more frequent in alcohol-positive patients (38.5% vs. 29.5%), increased with serum ethanol concentration, and was the strongest predictor of ICU treatment and mortality. Nearly one in three severely injured patients had detectable serum ethanol. After adjustment for confounders, alcohol was not independently associated with mortality or intensive care resource use, and no dose-response relationship was found for these outcomes. The more frequent ICU treatment of alcohol-positive patients appears to be explained by their distinct injury pattern, particularly the concentration-dependent increase in severe TBI.

articles.title: Author response to letter titled "Assessing MRI utility in pediatric tibial-sided PCL avulsion fractures: the reference standard matters".
Anaesthesiologists Under Strain: Burnout and Its Associated Factors in a Conflict-affected Context, a Cross-sectional Study.
articles.journal: Turkish journal of anaesthesiology and reanimation
articles.abstract: Anaesthesiologists are particularly vulnerable to burnout due to extended working hours, high-pressure situations, limited patient interactions, multiple responsibilities, and inherent tensions in relationships with surgeons and administrators. The study aimed to explore burnout levels and the factors associated with them among anaesthesiologists in a conflict-affected setting. A cross-sectional study was carried out between May 2024 and August 2025 using a voluntary, anonymous, and electronic survey. The Copenhagen Burnout Inventory, demographics, and practice environment questions were included. Statistical analyses were conducted to identify factors associated with personal, work-related, and client-related burnout. A significance threshold of 0.05 was applied. Among the 82 anaesthesiologists, 57% experienced personal burnout, 51% experienced work-related burnout, and 28% experienced client-related burnout. Positive and significant associations were observed between working longer hours and personal burnout (adjusted ß [95% confidence interval (CI)]=15.6 (0.88; 30.3); P=0.04) and work-related burnout [adjusted ß (95% CI)=17.7 (3.68; 31.7); P=0.01], as well as between covering five or more night shifts per month and client-related burnout [adjusted ß (95% CI)=15.3 (3.86; 26.7); P=0.009]. The findings reveal concerning levels of burnout among anaesthesiologists in conflict-affected regions, which is particularly important given the ongoing regional conflict and limited conflict-specific data, and highlight the potential role of modifiable predictors and associated factors. Targeted interventions are essential to support anaesthesiologists' well-being and ensure the effective functioning of healthcare institutions in such settings. Future studies with larger, randomly selected samples are warranted to further explore this issue.
